questions.question: Siblings out of sync, a todo didn't update, a handler fires during render, or search shows old results — what's the diagnosis?
questions.title: React Debug Scenarios
questions.direct_answer: Four classic React bugs with their signatures: (1) SIBLINGS OUT OF SYNC — each holds its own copy of the state; fix by lifting to the nearest common parent (one owner, props down, events up) — never sync copies with effects. (2) TODO DIDN'T UPDATE — mutation: state.items.push() keeps the same array reference, Object.is sees no change, React skips the render; fix with immutable updates (items = [...items, next]) or the functional form. (3) HANDLER FIRES DURING RENDER — you wrote onClick={save()} instead of onClick={save} — the parens CALL it while rendering; pass the function, or wrap it when args are needed (onClick={() => save(id)}). (4) SEARCH SHOWS OLD RESULTS — a race: slow first response resolves after the fast second and overwrites it; fix with an epoch guard (ignore stale), AbortController (cancel), or serialize the queries.

sections.title: Interview Answer
Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    SYM{symptom} -->|siblings disagree| S1[two copies of the same state]
    S1 --> F1[lift to the lowest common parent — one owner]
    SYM -->|UI didn't update| S2[mutated state — same reference]
    S2 --> F2[new array/object or functional setState]
    SYM -->|runs on render not click| S3['onClick={fn()} — called during render']
    S3 --> F3['pass fn, or arrow-wrap when args needed']
    SYM -->|results are old| S4[race: slow first response overwrites fresh]
    S4 --> F4[epoch guard + AbortController — only newest renders]
    DELAY[adding setTimeout delays] -.masks, never fixes.-> S4
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The stale-closure family (why bug 2's functional form is the deeper answer): every render closes over ITS OWN props/state — a handler created in render N sees render N's values forever. When events fire later (a delayed save, an interval, an async callback), they may act on a snapshot. The functional update (setTodos(t => [...t, item])) receives the CURRENT queue state from React, not the captured one — it's the fix whenever the next value depends on the last value. Same family: useEffect deps that omit the used variable (the effect closes over the old one forever); the eslint exhaustive-deps rule exists to catch precisely this.

The sibling-state ladder (bug 1's full toolbox): (1) lift to parent — the default, works until the tree grows; (2) context — cross-cutting values (theme, auth) without drilling, but every consumer re-renders on change; (3) component-level store slices (Zustand/Jotai) — subscribe by selector so only the components reading the changed slice render; (4) URL state for shareable/survivable facts (filters, tabs, wizard steps — the search-params pattern). The diagnostic question for ANY sync bug: 'who owns this fact?' — if the answer is more than one component, that's the bug.

The race-condition toolbox in order of preference (bug 4's professional close): (a) AbortController — cancels the previous request at the transport layer (fetch takes signal; the aborted fetch rejects with AbortError you must catch-and-ignore); (b) epoch/sequence tokens — language-level, works when you can't abort (websockets, non-fetch APIs); (c) request serialization (a queue that runs one search at a time) — correctness over freshness, right when the backend can't handle concurrent queries; (d) server components/streaming (React 18 useTransition + startTransition for non-urgent updates keeps the OLD UI visible while the new one loads — 'keep showing stale rather than flash empty' is itself a UX pattern). The interview close: 'guard by identity (epoch), cancel by transport (abort), and let the framework decide urgency (transition) — in that order.'
